message.content:
Let the projection of \(\mathbf{a}\) onto \(P\) be
\[
\mathbf{x}=p\mathbf{b}+q\mathbf{c}.
\]
Since \(\mathbf{x}\) is the projection onto the plane spanned by \(\mathbf{b},\mathbf{c}\), the vector \(\mathbf{a}-\mathbf{x}\) is orthogonal to both \(\mathbf{b}\) and \(\mathbf{c}\).

Thus,
\[
(\mathbf{a}-p\mathbf{b}-q\mathbf{c})\cdot \mathbf{b}=0
\]
and
\[
(\mathbf{a}-p\mathbf{b}-q\mathbf{c})\cdot \mathbf{c}=0.
\]

Using the given dot products:
\[
\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{b}=\frac15,\qquad \mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{c}=\frac16,\qquad \mathbf{b}\cdot\mathbf{c}=\frac12,
\]
and \(\mathbf{b}\cdot\mathbf{b}=\mathbf{c}\cdot\mathbf{c}=1\), we get
\[
\frac15-p-\frac12q=0
\]
and
\[
\frac16-\frac12p-q=0.
\]
So
\[
p+\frac12q=\frac15,
\]
\[
\frac12p+q=\frac16.
\]

Solving,
\[
p=\frac{7}{45},\qquad q=\frac{4}{45}.
\]

The answer is \(\left(\frac{7}{45},\frac{4}{45}\right)\).
